citeAs: Gao, J., Gan, L., Li, Y., Ye, Y., & Wang, D. (2024). Dissecting Dissonance: Benchmarking Large Multimodal Models Against Self-Contradictory Instructions. arXiv preprint arXiv:2408.01091.
creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Fudan University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory)
description: The Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) benchmark evaluates the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) in recognizing conflicting commands. It comprises 20,000 conflicts, evenly distributed between language and vision paradigms.
name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
publisher: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Fudan University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
rai:dataCollection: Constructed using a novel automatic dataset creation framework, AutoCreate, which builds a multimodal cycle based on programs and large language models. It requires a small batch of manually input seeds to automatically generate a large quantity of high-quality, diverse data by LLMs.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The SemanticConflict task uses the ImageNet dataset to retrieve images according to a label.
rai:dataLimitations: Only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms. No fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree. Does not provide a detailed study on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For V-L conflicts, the image caption is modified to introduce a conflict. For FigureConflict, numerical data is manipulated by changing the maximum value to the minimum value, and a chart is plotted based on the altered data. For GeometricConflict, a phrase describing an object is modified to refer to a non-existent object. For SemanticConflict, the correct label in questions is substituted with similar but different objects.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Provides researchers and practitioners with a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies. The AutoCreate framework facilitates the creation of diverse instruction datasets, promoting inclusivity in AI research. By improving dissonance detection, the approach boosts LMM performance and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems, essential for societal integration.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to detect conflicted instructions.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large Language Models (LLMs) are used in the AutoCreate framework to automatically generate data, create self-contradictions, and double-check the quality of the generated dataset.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: Dataset is automatically generated by LLMs, not manually annotated per item.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No human annotators used for dataset creation.
